main_text.p: התפקד hithpakkéd. Hîc literæ Bach-lam ב be, כ ke, ל le, מ me, adduntur.

p.i: Hactenus dictum est de vocibus Nu-meri, videlicet de Nomine & Verbo: sequuntur voces sine numero, nempe Ad-verbium & Conjunctio.

main_text.head: DE ADVERBIO.
main_text.p: ADverbium est vox sine numero, quæ alicui voci adjuncta, circunstantiam ejus una voce effert, ut פּה po, vel פּא po, & בָּזֶה bazé, hîc שָׁם scham, ibi, illic, istic. הֵנָּה henna, & שָׁמָּה schámma, illuc, istuc. מָחָר machar & מָחֳרָת machoráth, cras. בֹּקֶר bóker, mane עֶרֶב ereb, vesperi, לֹא lo, vel אֵין en, אַיִן Ajin, בַּל bal, בְּלִי beli, בְּלֹא belo, בִּלְתִּי bilti, id est, non, nequaquam. בֹּא kó, ita. כֵּן ken & כַּךְ kach, & בְּכֵן bechen, sic. הֵא he & הֵן hen, en. הִנֵּה himné, ecce. לוּ lu vel לוּא lu, utinâ. אַחַר achár, postea.

page.notes: The Hebrew vowel points and dagesh marks are copied as far as legible; small points in the scan may differ slightly from the printed originals. The "ct" in "dictum" is a ligature in the print. The printed "Ajin" and the Hebrew forms in the body are reproduced as seen.
